issues.description: The problem statement defines Genre as having a String property named `name` and an optional `subgenre`. In the solution, the Genre struct declares the property as `genreName` while the Client code constructs and accesses Genre using `name` (e.g. `Genre(name: ...)` and `genre.name`). This mismatch between the struct field name (`genreName`) and the usages/expectation (`name`) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct identifier to use.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the identifier for the genre name consistent. Preferred fixes:
1) Rename the Genre struct property to `name` to match the problem statement and existing Client usage: `let name: String` (replace `genreName`).
OR
2) Update all usages and initializers in Client and elsewhere to use `genreName` (e.g. `Genre(genreName: "...", subgenre: ...)` and `genre.genreName`).
Either approach will restore consistency and prevent compilation errors; the first option (using `name`) best matches the problem specification.
